resources.string: Registering with the supernode over TCP
Stopped by itself: see the log
Scan the QR code of a network, made with n3n-qr or shown by another phone, or write its configuration.
The address of this phone in the network is no IPv4 address: address = 10.1.2.3/24 in [tuntap], or none, and the supernode hands one out.
This phone has no name yet: description = … in [connection]
Route all traffic through a peer
Exit peer: its address in the network
DNS server, reached through the exit peer

The exit peer needs filter.allow_routing = true in its configuration, IP forwarding and NAT (masquerade) towards the internet. IPv6 is held back meanwhile, so that nothing goes around the exit peer. Applies on the next connect.
Enter the exit peer\'s address in the network (e.g. 10.1.2.1)

The configuration, as in a .conf file of n3n:

[community]
name = mynetwork
key = mysecret
supernode = sn.example.org:7654

[tuntap]
address = 10.1.2.3/24

Each device needs an address of its own in the network: address = … in [tuntap], or none, and the supernode hands one out. Saved when you leave this screen; a running connection takes it on the next connect.
Saved: connect again to use it
Point the camera at the QR code of the configuration
No QR code found in that image
That QR code holds no n3n configuration
Replace the configuration with the one from the QR code?
If this is a protected n3n configuration, enter its PIN.
Not the right PIN, or no n3n code
The code holds this phone\'s address %1$s: the device that scans it has to change it to one of its own.
The device that scans it adds an address of its own (or lets the supernode assign one, where it can).
The code then shows neither the configuration nor that it is n3n\'s. Tell the PIN separately. A short PIN keeps a code from saying what it is at a glance; it is no strong protection.
Scan with the n3n app. The code holds the configuration as it is, key included: show it only to who may join.
Protected with a PIN. Scan with the n3n app, then enter the PIN.
The configuration does not fit into a QR code
